clue.text: How to get bread in, not together

parts.note: the clue words ask how to arrive at the phrase bread in: scatter a word whose letters are those of bread in

explanation.surface: Instructions on getting a loaf into the house, delivered in a muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, SCATTER (rearrange) BRAINED, and the result is BREAD IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disorganised and forgetful is far from collected, an informal synonym for a muddled person.

clue.text: What minimises exposed area as fine courtesans get changed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Elegant courtesans changing their clothes, oddly framed as a physics lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics this property makes a liquid's surface contract to the smallest possible area, as in round droplets.

clue.text: Forgetting how exciting cinemas can be

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters of the word cinemas are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that films are so thrilling they make you forget everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how' and 'can be' are link words around the anagram signal 'exciting'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for memory loss, used of someone suffering amnesia, so forgetting in the adjectival sense.

clue.text: Very pretty linnet finally produces a call

parts.note: twee means excessively pretty or quaint, a British usage

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word linnet

explanation.surface: A lovely little songbird ends by singing out.
explanation.definitionFit: A short chirp is the call of a small bird, the classic sound a linnet would make.

clue.text: Was promoted; would say was cabinet material

parts.note: rose, as in rose through the ranks

indicators.note: say signals that the following word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: the word would, pronounced like a timber term

explanation.surface: A politician promoted to the cabinet, with a stray remark about what he would say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabinet' suggests government, following on from 'promoted', but here it is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark tropical hardwood prized by furniture makers for fine cupboards and veneers.

clue.text: Credit record's going for nothing in course

indicators.note: one thing going in place of another signals a swap of letters

parts.note: a route is a course taken
nothing is the round letter O, like zero
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A financial track record changed for nothing in the middle of a course.
explanation.walkthrough: In ROUTE the O (nothing) is replaced by EP (a record) to give REPUTE; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is good name or reputation, the same sense as credit in giving someone credit for honesty.

clue.text: Just one member keen on war, not the leader

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the opening letter is dropped from the word meant

parts.note: martial means warlike

explanation.surface: Only one politician is hawkish, though not the party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the leader' removes M from MARTIAL to leave ARTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair and even-handed, which is what an unbiased judge is.

clue.text: Wife once in the past raised my way of choosing her?

parts.note: an ex is a former wife

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ago means in the past
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's former wife, and how he once chose her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AGO into OGA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The custom of marrying outside one's own tribe or group is a system for selecting a wife.

clue.text: Are you aware of DJ hunting song?

definitions.meaning: read literally, do you know a famous radio disc jockey, the late John Peel of the BBC, in Cumbrian dialect
a traditional English folk song about a Cumberland huntsman

explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a long-serving BBC radio disc jockey; ken means know in Scots and northern dialect, and ye is you.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cumbrian folk song's title asks do you know John Peel, also the name of a BBC Radio 1 disc jockey.

clue.text: Bean soup, nothing less, for seconds

parts.note: a runner is a climbing bean

indicators.note: less signals taking a letter away from the word soup

parts.note: nothing is the round letter O, like zero

explanation.surface: A diner asking for runner bean soup as a second helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like more food, but it means those finishing second.
explanation.definitionFit: Those placed second in a contest are the people who just miss first place.

clue.text: Bloom unknown to farm labourer

parts.note: a peon is a Latin American agricultural labourer
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A flower whose name a farmhand has never heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: A large showy garden flower, so a bloom in the gardener's sense.

clue.text: So posed, one liable to be stripped?

parts.note: as means so, in the sense of in that way
set means posed, as a question set or posed

explanation.surface: A model posing, and someone likely to undress.
explanation.walkthrough: Asset-stripping is buying a company to sell off its valuable parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Asset-stripping sells off a company's holdings, so a holding of value is something liable to be stripped.

clue.text: Security device, on paper, with a name: Lifeboat

parts.note: a term is a name for something
Noah's Ark saved its passengers from the Flood

explanation.surface: A security feature on documents linked to a named lifeboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifeboat' looks like a name, but it is Noah's Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint design in paper seen against light, used to deter forgery of banknotes.

clue.text: Hardly fast food: set out to eat a load

indicators.note: to eat means to take something inside
out signals the letters of the word set are rearranged

parts.note: cargo is a load carried

explanation.surface: Diners eating a lot of food that is hardly a quick snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' suggests quick service, but snails are famously slow; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails as a French dish: slow creatures and slow food, the opposite of fast food.

clue.text: Opera set up that's good to keep interest to the end

parts.note: to rig is to set up, as with equipment or a fixed result
ole is a cry of approval, Spanish for bravo

indicators.note: keep means to hold something within

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to the end signals the last letter of the word interest

explanation.surface: An opera production designed to hold the audience's attention to the finale.
explanation.walkthrough: TO keeps T, the final letter of 'interest', giving TTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera about a court jester, first performed in Venice in 1851.

clue.text: Trimmed tropical climber held by African

indicators.note: held by the trimmed vine, as something gripped is enclosed, so the word by sits inside it
trimmed means cut short, dropping the last letter

parts.note: a liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vine trimmed back by someone from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African' could be the definition of a noun or adjective; here it is a noun, a person from that country.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Libya, a country in North Africa, is a particular kind of African.

clue.text: Chap givin' handout that has strings attached

parts.note: a chap is a man
doling out, with the final g dropped in the same colloquial way as givin'

explanation.surface: A man handing out charity, with strings attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings attached' looks like conditions on charity, but means a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute-like stringed instrument, plucked with a plectrum, has strings fixed along its neck.

clue.text: Leaderless troops need gesture, from him?

definitions.text: Leaderless troops need gesture, from him?

indicators.note: leaderless drops the opening letter of the word meant

parts.note: men is a common word for troops
a sign is a gesture

explanation.surface: Soldiers without a commander look to a junior officer for a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' takes M off MEN to leave EN; the whole clue also describes a junior officer leading troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a junior officer, historically a standard-bearer, to whom troops look for a signal.

clue.text: Escape -— read about it elsewhere

definitions.meaning: a slow leak of liquid, such as fluid seeping out
the instruction to look at another page of the text, as in a cross-reference

explanation.definitionFit: A gradual leak is an escape of fluid; split in two, the word is a cross-reference instruction to look at a page.

clue.text: Cover for tomb briefly cheers architect

parts.note: a pall is a cloth spread over a coffin or tomb

indicators.note: briefly means cut short by the last letter

parts.note: cheers and adios both mean goodbye

explanation.surface: A tomb's covering briefly lifts the mood of its architect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' looks like celebration but is the British farewell; 'briefly' trims ADIOS to ADIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Palladio was an Italian Renaissance architect whose villas inspired Palladian style.

clue.text: Picture success as transvestite?

indicators.note: as here is read as success being in the dress of a transvestite, inside the other word

parts.note: drag is cross-dressing, the costume of a transvestite
a win is a success

explanation.surface: Picture someone succeeding in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as success while dressed as a transvestite, which is exactly the container: the win sits in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch made with pencil or pen is a picture, the simplest form of art.

clue.text: Remitted large sum I have banked

indicators.note: banked means deposited and kept within

parts.note: a wad is a large bundle of money
I've is the short form of I have

explanation.surface: Someone who has banked a large sum of money has let a debt go.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive a fee or rule is to remit it, giving up the claim to it, as with a waived charge.

clue.text: Team of beaters move silently, forbidden to speak

indicators.note: to speak signals that the words are said out loud, giving words with the same sound

parts.note: to steal is to move quietly, as in to steal away; banned means forbidden

explanation.surface: Beaters at a shoot creep about quietly, forbidden to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaters' suggests a game-shoot, but it means players who beat steel drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean ensemble of steel drums, played by striking them with sticks, is a team of drummers.

clue.text: Downfall, having previously good character

indicators.note: having previously places the second piece ahead of the first

parts.note: rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: A ruin that befalls someone who was once of good character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' looks like ruin but is rain, a fall of water from above.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is the texture or nature of something, as in going against the grain of one's character.

clue.text: City page — no ads admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let inside: the letters sit within the words page no ads

explanation.surface: A city newspaper page that carries no advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian port city in Liguria, birthplace of Columbus.

clue.text: No role for abstract painting

parts.note: O, the round letter, is nothing or no
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A remark that abstract art leaves no part to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of abstract art using geometric patterns to create optical illusions, popular in the 1960s.

clue.text: Saint's fast pointless? It has point

indicators.note: it has means contains the following piece within it

parts.note: vain means futile or pointless
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Is a saint's fast pointless? It has some point.
explanation.walkthrough: VAIN plus E holds LENT: VA-LENT-IN-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Valentine is the Roman martyr whose feast on 14 February honours lovers.

clue.text: Biographer whose work is out of this world

definitions.text: Biographer whose work is out of this world

parts.words: Biographer whose work is out of this world
parts.note: a heavenly being who writes down every person's deeds, chronicling lives from beyond the earth

explanation.definitionFit: In Christian and Jewish tradition a heavenly scribe keeps a record of each person's good and bad actions.
